PR.title: Require exact owner authority for Rook-only native delivery
PR.body:
## Summary

Separate immutable source authorship from delivery execution. Only authenticated principal rook / GitHub bot 345406391, explicitly configured with deliver capability and bound to an owner-approved exact-artifact handoff, can receive or execute native v3 delivery. Authors, engineering reviewers and QA actors cannot merge even with delivery_hold disabled. Source/task/assignment provenance and independent exact-head peer/QA gates remain immutable. Selection, checkout preparation, action execution, merge confirmation, completion and original-request journal recovery enforce the separate delivery role. Release authority stays separate.

## Independent review fixes

Addresses Robin's two changes-requested findings on 96ab03dce7809db8a9230f781269157d5868501c:

1. Owner withdrawal now authenticates current owner read/decide and historical thread membership, then binds exactly to a recorded owner grant. It does not require the authority being withdrawn to remain executable. Pause/resume, disabled/re-enabled Rook, rejected/superseded goals and stale assignments cannot revive the withdrawn grant. New grants retain all current execution-authority checks. Revocation appends a higher monotonic sequence; original decisions and idempotency receipts remain intact.
2. Handoff discovery retains all decisions without eagerly reading private evidence. Live and cached readers hydrate only current nonrevoked candidate evidence; inaccessible current evidence denies that candidate rather than aborting unrelated work. Revoked/superseded owner evidence and revoked QA-report history are not global discovery prerequisites. Tests exercise two still-approved goals with independently scoped evidence access, repeated polls, supersession, revocation, current inaccessible evidence and changed private report contents. No fallback to an older grant is admitted.

## Verification

Required local and remote base remains d5d8dea1f0f71a81176c4f1eda94dcf8e06b642a on simplify/operational-cleanup. Configured Flox; Go 1.26.10, Python 3.14.7, existing GCC 15.3.0 wrapper with CGO_ENABLED=1 for race tests. PASS full go test ./..., full go test -race ./..., build, vet, gofmt, golangci-lint v2.12.2 (zero issues), govulncheck v1.6.0 (no vulnerabilities), diff check and all 58 Python CI packaging/installer/artifact tests. Go permission fixtures use umask 022 and dropped DAC override capabilities. One concurrent full non-race rerun encountered an unmodified TestNativeTerminalWaitAllowsConversation TempDir cleanup error (directory not empty); the subsequent standalone full suite passed. Full race also passed. Previous head's hosted test and lint passed; those receipts do not clear this changed head. New exact-head CI, renewed Robin review and separate Wren exact-artifact QA remain required.

## Explicit limitations and activation boundary

Owner-authored PR158 remains 99587865a8133a67311dcb1b65e67a59562eedb5 against main; stacked PR159 remains d5d8dea1f0f71a81176c4f1eda94dcf8e06b642a against simplify/kata-first. Native intake still requires bot authorship, registered task/PR association and v3 provenance. There is no supported external-owner review/QA admission operation. No owner impersonation, metadata invention, replacement implementation, stack rewrite or PR157-smoke-as-runtime-clearance is included. Adding deliver changes the roster digest; cross-policy/new-goal evidence carry-forward and rebinding already-published Kata assignments remain unsupported and must stop for supported authority disposition.

Operator build/config/grant activation and rollback packet: docs/rook-only-delivery.md, including durable withdrawal semantics. Source publication only: no install/restart, real config/grant activation, hold lifting, credential borrowing, merge, release, compatibility-removal or retention changes. Existing AUTHOR-bound policy must not bootstrap its own replacement. Only a separately activated, assigned Rook delivery stage may merge after all gates; this author has no merge authority.

Reviews.body:
Independent engineering review of exact head 96ab03dce7809db8a9230f781269157d5868501c against required base d5d8dea1f0f71a81176c4f1eda94dcf8e06b642a. Changes needed for two reproduced control-plane defects. Hawk is the source author; this is Robin's assigned peer review, not QA or delivery clearance.

1. [P2] Allow owner withdrawal while the goal/executor is disabled. internal/master/handoffs.go:119-122 calls deliveryAuthority for revocations as well as grants; that function requires a currently enabled Rook at lines 190-195. The earlier a.Valid/fresh.Valid gates also reject withdrawal while a goal is paused. Reproduction using deliveryFixture: create grant G, pause the goal (or remove Rook's read capability), submit the exact G fields with revoked=true and a new request ID, then resume/re-enable. Revocation returns forbidden, and TaskComplete using original G succeeds after re-enable. Both independent overlay cases fail on this exact head. This prevents durable withdrawal during a disabled/recovery window and leaves the old decision able to revive. Authenticate/authorize the owner and bind withdrawal to the original recorded authority, but do not require the authority being withdrawn to remain executable. Add regression coverage for pause/resume and disabled/re-enabled Rook, preserving immutable history and latest-decision ordering.

2. [P2] Do not make inaccessible revoked history a global discovery prerequisite. internal/worker/native_handoffs.go:81-87 eagerly fetches the evidence message of every delivery handoff, including revoked/superseded history, and propagates one forbidden read out of the entire catalog. Reproduction: valid deliverable goal B plus still-approved historical goal A; A's grant is revoked, then Rook loses membership in A's separate QA evidence thread while retaining source-thread membership. The revoked handoff is still listed, but its evidence read fails. Both live and cached catalog loading abort before unrelated B can be selected. An independent worker overlay starts from nativeDeliveryReadyFixture, adds an unrelated revoked decision whose evidence returns forbidden, and reproduces this catalog failure. Preserve decisions for latest-grant/revocation ordering, but scope evidence hydration/denial to executable candidates so historical access removal cannot stall unrelated authorized work. Add a multi-goal regression with revoked inaccessible evidence and a valid candidate.

Validation: clean assigned checkout; live task binding and PR head/base verified. Configured Flox, Go 1.26.10 linux/arm64, Python 3.14.7. PASS full go test ./..., full go test -race ./..., go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt listing empty, git diff --check, govulncheck v1.6.0 (no vulnerabilities), and all 58 Python packaging/installer/artifact tests. Permission fixtures used umask 022 and dropped DAC override capabilities; race used existing GCC 15.3.0 wrapper and CGO_ENABLED=1. Hosted exact-head CI test and lint both PASS. Local golangci-lint is unavailable; hosted lint is the lint receipt. Independent external overlay probes TestRobin161RevokeWhileDisabled/{paused,rook-disabled} and TestRobin161InaccessibleRevokedHistory FAIL as described; implementation and committed tests were not modified.

The documented unsupported owner-authored PR158/159 admission and cross-policy evidence carry-forward paths are explicit limitations, not invented native clearance. No source edits, install/restart/config activation, merge, hold lifting, QA verdict, release or replacement task was performed. Hawk should fix these defects within the assigned task and republish; the changed head requires renewed independent review and separate Wren exact-artifact QA.

Independent Robin engineering re-review of exact head e55da25979087dfb16ef23226263435c14c45fe9 against required base d5d8dea1f0f71a81176c4f1eda94dcf8e06b642a. Both prior P2 findings are resolved; no new blocking findings. Reviewed the complete corrective delta from 96ab03dce7809db8a9230f781269157d5868501c, preserving the earlier review of the bounded Rook-only policy. Fresh task binding, source author, PR head and approved base verified; checkout remains clean.

Withdrawal now authenticates current owner read/decide authority and historical source/QA thread membership, requires an exact recorded owner grant, and appends an immutable higher-sequence decision without depending on current goal/executor/task-provider eligibility. It does not turn the withdrawal path into a grant path. Original request identity, mismatch rejection and latest-decision semantics remain intact. My original independent TestRobin161RevokeWhileDisabled overlay now passes unchanged for both paused/resumed goal and disabled/re-enabled Rook; the original grant cannot complete after withdrawal. Added production regressions also cover rejected/superseded goals, stale assignments, exact input matching and live owner-authority denial.

Discovery retains decision history but no longer eagerly hydrates revoked/superseded private evidence. Current owner and QA evidence is freshly read; missing/inaccessible/changed current evidence denies only that candidate, without older-grant fallback. Reviewed both live and cached projections and latest-decision extraction. My original independent TestRobin161InaccessibleRevokedHistory overlay now passes unchanged. New two-goal live/cached tests exercise revoked/superseded history, current inaccessible evidence, private report drift and repeated polls without reusing stale private clearance. New withdrawal/evidence regression groups pass five repetitions.

Independent exact-head validation in configured Flox, Go 1.26.10 linux/arm64, Python 3.14.7: PASS full go test ./... on rerun, full go test -race ./..., go build ./..., go vet ./..., empty gofmt listing, git diff --check, govulncheck v1.6.0 (no vulnerabilities), and all 58 Python packaging/installer/artifact tests. Root permission fixtures used umask 022 and dropped DAC override capabilities; race used CGO_ENABLED=1 and the existing GCC 15.3.0 wrapper. Validation caveat: the first non-race full run concurrent with the race suite reproduced the reported unmodified TestNativeTerminalWaitAllowsConversation TempDir cleanup failure (directory not empty); subsequent full non-race rerun and full race suite passed. This intermittent fixture cleanup remains a residual test risk, not a newly attributed policy defect. Local golangci-lint is unavailable; exact-head hosted lint passed. Hosted test CI was still pending at the last check and is not represented here as passed.

This is independent exact-head engineering approval only, not Wren QA, delivery authorization or activation clearance. The source-bundle-v1 metadata binds this head to digest 8c206e9e3fe590dd6a1e861fcd122b453ac4aa00b6b8e16934c2680e9d1c5f6e. Owner-authored PR158/159 native review/QA admission and cross-policy/new-goal evidence carry-forward remain explicitly unsupported; no fabricated binding or historical smoke evidence clears them. Separate Wren exact-artifact QA, current CI and all owner/operator activation and native Rook delivery gates remain required. No source edits, install/restart/config activation, hold lifting, merge, release, credential borrowing or replacement task was performed.
